analysis:
Examined both files' metadata, complete supplied action source, workflow base excerpt and every workflow patch hunk. The composite action adds SwiftPM repository caching keyed by OS, workspace/home layout, lane and lockfiles (action.yml head 47–53). Cache writes now default off and require explicit opt-in (107, 116, 143); ci.yml supplies that opt-in only for master/dev pushes (head 19 and the changed callers). Audio and cluster metadata cache writes receive the same restriction. This reduces PR cache writes; no supported cache-poisoning regression was identified.
The workflow introduces shallow/full-history .git cache families, connectivity checking before checkout, disabled credential persistence, sparse checkout outside Docs Lint, and partial-clone full history (ci.yml head 57–93, 163–197 and repeated later hunks). Saves occur immediately after checkout, before repository build/test scripts. Connectivity checking is not authentication of Git config, hooks or refs, but the supplied evidence does not establish an adversarial writer to caches restored by trusted runs. No credential leak or attacker-controlled execution can therefore be reported from this scope.
Relevant integrity contracts include A-017/T-054 and A-011/T-013/T-034; this change affects CI inputs, not serving authorization or signed-artifact qualification directly. T-041 concerns inference KV caching, not these build caches; its encryption, scope and TTL controls are unchanged. No runtime prompt exposure, billing or attestation change is visible.
Integration should reconcile the new .git and SwiftPM cache producers/consumers with any other supplied workflow changes, particularly cache namespaces and trusted-write eligibility. Also verify scripts that derive identity/provenance from Git refs tolerate restored refs; ci.yml head 920 explicitly removes describe text from one cluster key. Those scripts and the checkout implementation were not supplied, so provenance correctness remains an unverified contract, not a finding.
